subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In a longitudinal wave, in which direction do the particles oscillate relative to the direction of energy transfer?
options: Perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer
Parallel to the direction of energy transfer
In a circular path around the source
questions.explain: In a longitudinal wave the oscillations are parallel to the direction in which the wave transfers energy, producing compressions and rarefactions.

questions.q: Which equation correctly relates wave speed (v), frequency (f) and wavelength (λ)?
questions.explain: The wave equation states that wave speed equals frequency multiplied by wavelength.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.explain: Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz), where one hertz is one wave cycle per second.

questions.q: What name is given to the maximum displacement of a wave from its rest position?
questions.explain: The amplitude is the maximum displacement of a point on the wave from its undisturbed (rest) position.

questions.q: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum has the longest wavelength?
questions.explain: Radio waves have the longest wavelength and lowest frequency of all the electromagnetic waves.

questions.q: At what speed do all electromagnetic waves travel through a vacuum?
questions.explain: All electromagnetic waves travel at approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s in a vacuum.

questions.q: Which of these electromagnetic waves has the highest frequency?
questions.explain: Gamma rays lie at the high-frequency, short-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: What is the approximate range of frequencies audible to a healthy young human ear?
questions.explain: The human audible range is roughly 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz (20 kHz).

questions.q: For a light ray reflecting off a plane mirror, how does the angle of incidence compare with the angle of reflection?
options: The angle of reflection is always larger
The angle of incidence is always larger
questions.explain: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal.

questions.q: In a transverse wave, which statement best describes the motion of the medium?
options: The oscillations are at right angles to the direction of energy transfer
The oscillations are along the direction of energy transfer
The particles move at the same speed as the wave
The medium is permanently displaced in the direction of travel
questions.explain: In a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular (at right angles) to the direction in which energy is transferred.

questions.q: Two sound waves have the same frequency, but one is louder than the other. Which property differs between them?
questions.explain: A louder sound carries more energy, which corresponds to a larger amplitude while the frequency stays the same.

questions.q: Why can sound waves not travel through a vacuum?
options: Sound needs particles in a medium to transmit vibrations
Sound waves are absorbed by a vacuum
A vacuum reflects all sound waves
Sound travels too slowly to cross a vacuum
questions.explain: Sound is a mechanical wave that requires particles of a medium to pass on the vibrations, so it cannot travel through a vacuum.

questions.q: Which use is most appropriate for microwaves?
questions.explain: Microwaves pass through the atmosphere and are widely used for satellite and mobile phone communications, as well as heating in ovens.

questions.q: Overexposure to which type of electromagnetic radiation from the Sun can cause skin cancer?
questions.explain: Ultraviolet radiation can damage skin cells and cause skin cancer, which is why sun-protection is important.

questions.q: Which application relies on infrared radiation?
options: Sterilising surgical instruments with gamma rays
questions.explain: Warm objects emit infrared radiation, so thermal imaging cameras detect infrared to form heat pictures.

questions.q: A ray of light passes from air into a glass block and slows down. What happens to the ray as it enters the glass?
options: It bends away from the normal
It continues in a straight line without bending
It reflects back into the air
questions.explain: When light slows down entering a denser medium such as glass, it refracts towards the normal.

questions.q: Total internal reflection can occur when light travels from glass to air only if the angle of incidence is:
options: Equal to 90° minus the critical angle
questions.explain: Total internal reflection happens when light travels from a denser to a less dense medium and the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.

questions.q: A water wave has a frequency of 20 Hz and a wavelength of 15 m. What is its speed?
questions.explain: Using v = f × λ: 20 × 15 = 300 m/s.

questions.q: A wave has a frequency of 50 Hz. What is its time period?
questions.explain: The period is the reciprocal of frequency: T = 1/f = 1/50 = 0.02 s.

questions.q: Light enters a transparent material with an angle of incidence of 40° and an angle of refraction of 25°. Using n = sin i / sin r, what is the refractive index (sin 40° = 0.643, sin 25° = 0.423)?
